title: Kernel policy simulator driven by sequence-length profiles
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: build a deterministic+stochastic simulator that consumes lightweight sequence-length (seqlen) histograms and microprofile signatures to evaluate kernel selection policies before rolling them to the runtime. The simulator should estimate p50/p95/p99 latency and cost for mixed prefill/decode workloads, surface stability risk (switch churn), and produce a ranked candidate list of kernel configurations with confidence intervals.

Why: Online autotuners can explore aggressively and cause oscillation for customers with heavy tail seqlen distributions. Existing profilers collect microbenchmarks but lack a fast way to predict how a policy will behave end-to-end under realistic request mixes (prefill+decode phases, KV cache hit rates, quantized fallback). A simulator enables offline policy validation, safer rollout, and more targeted exploration budgets per-customer or per-class.

Scope and features:
- Input formats: seqlen histogram sketches (per-route and global), microbenchmarks (kernel latency/cost per seqlen bucket), and current KV/cache hit distributions.
- Policy model: accepts a candidate kernel selection function (rules or learned scorer) and simulates request streams with configurable burstiness and concurrency.
- Prefill/decode modeling: explicit two-phase modeling that accounts for different kernel choices and warm KV effects between phases.
- Safety bands: compute churn and stability scores; simulate explicit safety fallback windows (e.g., prefer fallback kernel if latency > X ms for Y requests).
- Swap budget & hedging: simulate limited kernel swaps per-minute and hedging (dual-path) strategies and estimate unit-cost impact.
- Latency tail estimation: Monte Carlo sampling + analytical tail extrapolation for p99/p999 when sample sizes are small.
- Output: ranked candidate configs, latency/cost/confidence breakdowns, a diff view vs baseline policy, and per-route recommendations.
- Artifacts: a CLI simulator binary, a lightweight REST sandbox endpoint for the Console to run small sims, and a reproducible notebook harness for SRE/Models team.

Non-goals: full-fidelity GPU instruction-level emulation or replacing live A/B canaries. Simulator should be fast (minutes per-route) and conservative.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator can reproduce known regression from ENG-71234 benchmark within 10% of observed p95 latency on seeded traces.
- Produces ranked recommendations and a stability score for a given policy input.
- Integrates with telemetry to pull a seqlen sketch and run a default sim in <5 minutes for a single route.
- End-to-end PR with unit tests, CI, and an example console sandbox UI mock.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data ingestion: define seqlen-histogram proto and microbenchmark CSV schema (2 weeks).
2) Simulation core: event-driven request stream engine with prefilling/decoding states and kernel decision hook (3 weeks).
3) Analysis & estimators: Monte Carlo tail estimator + analytic extrapolator module (2 weeks).
4) Integrations: plugin to runtime to export sample traces, telemetry adapter, and Console sandbox API (2 weeks).
5) E2E validation: test against historical incidents/benchmarks and run customer-impacted route sims (1 week).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: simulator underestimates tail due to unmodeled contention. Mitigation: conservative bias factor and cross-check against short live canaries.
- Risk: noisy microbenchmarks. Mitigation: aggregate across time windows and attach confidence intervals to latency/cost estimates.
- Risk: too many false positives in recommendations. Mitigation: require a minimum sample threshold and require manual approval for P0 customers.

Success metrics:
- Reduced kernel-related rollout rollbacks by 50% in next quarter.
- Simulator recommendations adopted for >= 30% of runtime autotune changes during the trial.
